lede: Mentoring programme design gives HR, learning and talent professionals a structured way to formalize or scale workplace mentoring. For people-development practitioners, the course covers defining programme purpose and success measures, setting participant criteria and matching processes, and establishing governance and onboarding. Participants also develop communications, monitoring dashboards and an implementation plan to guide programme review and improvement.
audienceIntro: This Mentoring Programme Design and Implementation Training is tailored for professionals who already manage people-development initiatives and now need to design, formalize, or scale structured mentoring in their organization.
audience: Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Manager using
People Experience or Employee Engagement Lead
modules: Mentoring Programme Fundamentals and Strategic Rationale
Defining Purpose, Scope, and Success Metrics
Matching Processes, Agreements, and Relationship Support
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Simple Data Dashboards
Implementation Planning, Risk Management, and Continuous Improvement
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course designed for professionals who already work with learning, talent, HR, or people-development initiatives. You should have practical experience participating in or coordinating development programmes such as leadership programmes, graduate schemes, or coaching and mentoring initiatives. Familiarity with basic HR processes (such as performance management, succession planning, and learning needs analysis) is expected, but no statistical or technical background is required. You do not need coding or advanced analytics skills; all technology-related content focuses on operational application of off-the-shelf mentoring and survey tools. Advanced evaluation and data concepts are covered at conceptual and operational levels, not as hands-on technical engineering.
